record.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    The cDNA clone for a 10-deacetylbaccatin III-10-
                    <jats:italic>O</jats:italic>
                    -acetyl transferase, which catalyzes formation of the last diterpene intermediate in the Taxol biosynthetic pathway, has been isolated from
                    <jats:italic>Taxus cuspidata</jats:italic>
                    . By using consensus sequences from an assembly of transacylases of plant origin and from many deduced proteins of unknown function, a homology-based PCR cloning strategy was employed to amplify initially a 911-bp gene fragment of the putative taxane C-10 hydroxyl acetyl transferase from
                    <jats:italic>Taxus</jats:italic>
                    . This amplicon was used to screen a cDNA library constructed from mRNA isolated from methyl jasmonate-induced
                    <jats:italic>Taxus</jats:italic>
                    cells, from which the full-length 10-deacetylbaccatin III-10-
                    <jats:italic>O</jats:italic>
                    -transacetylase sequence was obtained. Expression of the ORF from pCWori
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    in
                    <jats:italic>Escherichia coli</jats:italic>
                    JM109 afforded a functional enzyme, as determined by
                    <jats:sup>1</jats:sup>
                    H-NMR and MS verification of the product baccatin III derived from 10-deacetylbaccatin III and acetyl CoA. The full-length cDNA has an ORF of 1,320 bp corresponding to a deduced protein of 440 residues with a calculated molecular weight of 49,052, consistent with the size of the operationally soluble, monomeric, native acetyl transferase. The recombinant acetyl transferase has a pH optimum of 7.5, has
                    <jats:italic>K</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>m</jats:sub>
                    values of 10 μM and 8 μM for 10-deacetylbaccatin III and acetyl CoA, respectively, and is apparently regiospecific toward the 10-hydroxyl group of the taxane ring. Amino acid sequence comparison of 10-deacetylbaccatin III-10-
                    <jats:italic>O</jats:italic>
                    -acetyl transferase with taxadienol-5-
                    <jats:italic>O</jats:italic>
                    -acetyl transferase and with other known acyl transferases of plant origin indicates a significant degree of similarity between these enzymes (80% and 64–67%, respectively).
                  </jats:p>
title: Molecular cloning of a 10-deacetylbaccatin III-10- O -acetyl transferase cDNA from Taxus and functional expression in Escherichia coli
